required_concepts: shape does not have to be a specific type
acceptable_paraphrases: A shape with two lines of symmetry does not necessarily have to be a rectangle
Not all shapes with two lines of symmetry are rectangles
Other quadrilaterals like rhombuses can also have exactly two lines of symmetry
critical_errors: stating or implying that only rectangles can have two lines of symmetry
misconceptions: all shapes with two lines of symmetry are rectangles
only a rectangle has two lines of symmetry
a shape must be a specific type to have two lines of symmetry (e.g., it must always be a rhombus)
lines of symmetry imply a right angle (90°)
grading_notes: Credit should be given for correct identification of shapes that can have two lines of symmetry, and for the understanding that not all such shapes are rectangles. Misconceptions about specific angles or exclusivity to rectangles should result in partial credit or no credit.
